  Beverly Hills City Council Liaison / Public Works Commission Meeting

  SPECIAL MEETING HIGHLIGHTS

  Thursday, January 25, 2024
  11:30 AM

MEETING CALLED TO ORDER
Date / Time:  January 25, 2024 / 11:30 AM

IN ATTENDANCE:  Vice Mayor Julian Gold MD, Councilmember Sharona Nazarian PYSD,
  Public Works Commission Chairperson John Millan, Public Works
  Commissioner Mark Nehoray, Public Works Director Shana Epstein,
  Environmental Compliance and Programs Manager Josette Descalzo,
  Executive Assistant Ilene Knebel

Mayor Gold proposed modifying the Agenda to take TAB 3 prior to TAB 2. There were no
objections.

1. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Members of the public will be given the opportunity to directly address the Committee on any item
  listed on the agenda.

  Speakers:  None

Taken out of order.

2. AMENDING THE ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS RELATING TO THE
  REMOVAL OF GROUNDWATER
  Environmental Compliance and Programs Manager Josette Descalzo gave a presentation on
  amending the dewatering ordinance. The proposed changes would remove the R-1 (single-
  family residential zone) exemption and would apply the requirements to use groundwater for
  beneficial use. Alternatively, new and substantially remodeled R-1 projects may pay a
  replenishment fee. Staff recommends removing the R-1 exemption and requiring the
  ordinance on new and substantially remodeled properties, as well as keeping the
  replenishment fee to drive beneficial-use analysis. The commission stressed the importance
  of communicating the benefits of these changes to the public as an incentive that pays for
  itself quickly and is the right thing to do; they also asked about finding better ways to collect
  the groundwater running downhill from this process that is not being collected or collecting in
  the streets or on sidewalks. The council liaison requested what services are available for
  homes not required under this ordinance to participate. The liaison also discussed finding
  better ways to educate residents in the canyons about the excess water that can cause issues
  in their neighborhood due to dewatering and asked about the quality of the shallow
  groundwater/how to prevent residents from drinking or using the untreated water. The
  commission and liaison ultimately voiced their support for amending the ordinance. The
  council also requested that staff investigate ways to collect the groundwater in reservoirs.
 3. PROPOSED ORDINANCE AMENDING THE BEVERLY HILLS MUNICIPAL CODE TO
  REGULATE POLYSTRENE FOODWARE AND PLASTIC WASTE
  Environmental Compliance and Programs Manager Josette Descalzo gave a presentation on
  the proposed ordinance aiming to reduce polystyrene foodware/plastic waste. Key provisions
  include the following: food facilities cannot distribute single-use articles that are neither
  compostable nor recyclable; retail establishments cannot sell expanded polystyrene products;
  third-party online food ordering businesses must allow food facilities to indicate which single-
  use foodware accessories they offer for customer selection; and full-service restaurants must
  provide multi-service utensils instead of single-use articles to dine-in customers. Beverages
  would not be regulated under this ordinance. He also gave an overview of the ordinance’s
  development, including extensive outreach efforts with the public and with businesses for their
  feedback and support. The ordinance would have a staggered implementation taking course
  over 1-2 years from the time of passing. Staff recommends moving forward with the ordinance
  for adoption by the end of the 1st quarter 2024. The commission voiced their support for the
  ordinance and recounted the efforts it took to create this current version of the ordinance. The
  council liaison asked about encouraging compliance with the businesses and ensuring that
  there was proper communication with the city’s food-related businesses, including
  translations. The council liaison also asked about the $500 assistance offered to businesses
  to purchase ordinance compliant products if their applications are approved.

  Speaker:  Public comment was heard from Todd Johnson.

4. ADJOURNMENT
  Date / Time:  January 25, 2024 / 12:25 PM
